claim: After Agnew's resignation, Nixon nominated House Minority Leader Gerald Ford as vice president on October 12, 1973. Ford became the first person ever appointed to the vice presidency under the 25th Amendment, confirmed by the Senate 92–3 and the House 387–35 and sworn in December 6, 1973. A decade earlier Ford had served on the Warren Commission investigating the assassination of John F. Kennedy, and in 1965 co-authored Portrait of the Assassin, a book defending the Warren Report. When Nixon resigned in August 1974, Ford — never elected to national office — became president.

sources.quote: After the resignation of vice president Agnew, Ford became the first person appointed to the vice presidency under the terms of the 25th Amendment. After President Nixon resigned in August 1974, Ford immediately assumed the presidency.
